title: Private Deployments: VPC & On-Prem Comprehensive Guide and Customer Requirements Library
author: Morgan Chen
body:
Overview:

This document is a consolidated reference for Redwood Inference private deployments (VPC-hosted and on-premises). It combines: reference architectures, packaging formats and installation artifacts, a customer requirements library, day-2 operations guidance (monitoring, backups, scaling), and tested upgrade & rollback procedures. It is intended for Solutions Engineering, Customer Ops, and SRE teams supporting private deployments.

Scope and audience:
- Audience: Solutions Engineers, Platform Engineers, Customer Site Reliability Engineers, Support Engineers.
- Scope: Production-ready deployments (single-tenant VPC and on-prem air-gapped), with emphasis on operational requirements and safe upgrades.

Summary of key recommendations:
- Use the VPC reference architecture for cloud-hosted private deployments unless the customer requires on-prem hardware or air-gapped operation.
- Deliver installation artifacts as both Helm chart and an OCI Docker bundle for flexibility. For air-gapped customers provide an OVA/OCI archive and a signed manifest.
- Minimum production hardware for inference nodes: 4x A100-style GPUs (or equivalent), 256GB RAM node for model serving, and at least two control-plane VMs (2 vCPU, 8GB) for agent orchestration.
- SLOs to communicate: 99.9% availability per service, 95th-percentile latency < 200ms for short generator workloads (<=512 tokens) on Dedicated GPU pools.

1) Supported deployment modes and recommended use cases:
- VPC-managed private deployment (customer VPC with Redwood control plane connectors): recommended for customers that need cloud isolation with managed control plane.
- Self-hosted VPC (control plane in-customer VPC using our control-plane connector): for customers who require full network control but want Redwood managed updates.
- On-prem (air-gapped / offline): for regulated workloads requiring no egress.
- Hybrid (on-prem compute, cloud control plane via direct connect/VPN): for customers who need low latency local inference with centralized billing & telemetry.

2) Reference architectures (high level):
- VPC Reference Architecture (recommended):
  - Components: customer VPC (subnets: mgmt, control, compute), NAT gateway, transit gateway/Direct Connect for cross-region routing, Redis or Memorystore for KV cache (managed), S3-compatible object store for model artifacts, Customer KMS + HSM for key management.
  - Services: model-serving pods (GPU nodes), control-plane agents (scale 2+), logging (fluentd -> ELK/CloudWatch), metrics (Prometheus remote write), tracer (Jaeger/OTel).
  - Networking: private subnets for compute, route tables with SG rules: control-plane agent -> port 8443 (TLS), model-serving -> ports 8000/8080 for internal telemetry, NTP outbound restricted to approved time servers.

- On-Prem Air-Gapped Reference Architecture:
  - Components: local object registry (OCI), internal artifact repository (Nexus/Artifactory), local Redis cluster for KV cache (replicated), NTP appliance, per-cluster PKI + offline-signed manifests.
  - Packaging: pre-signed OCI tarballs, signed manifest.json, verification script (sha256).
  - Isolation: no outbound egress on compute nodes; upstream pulls coordinated by site admin via provided offline mirror tools.

3) Customer requirements library (checklist to verify before engagement):
- Organization & people:
  - Deployment owner / point of contact (name, email, phone).
  - Engineering contact for networking & security.
  - On-call rotation for site SREs (escalation matrix).

- Networking & Security requirements:
  - VPC subnets planned and available: public mgmt subnet / private compute subnets.
  - CIDR expectations and peering/transit connectivity documented.
  - KMS/HSM availability and key provisioning plan.
  - Firewall rules allowing outbound to Redwood control-plane endpoints (list provided).
  - TLS PKI (customer-provided certs or Redwood-signed), root CA pinning for air-gapped installs.

- Compute & Storage requirements:
  - GPU profile: preferred (NVIDIA A100 80GB or equivalent), fallback options (A100 40GB, H100, or multi-GPU small nodes).
  - Minimum cluster size: 4 inference GPUs for production (single shard), prefer 8+ for production-onboarding at scale.
  - Disk: model cache tier (local NVMe 2TB+ per node), logs (separate EBS/NFS) with retention policy.
  - Object store: S3-compatible with lifecycle for model artifacts; snapshot schedule.

- Operational & Compliance:
  - Backup windows and retention for config and critical state.
  - Audit logging requirements (RDS/ELK/CloudTrail or on-prem equivalent).
  - Data residency constraints and approved regions.

4) Packaging & installer artifacts:
- Distribution formats delivered:
  - Helm chart (stable) with values.yaml examples.
  - OCI Docker images (signed).
  - Air-gapped bundle: OCI archive + manifest + verification tool.
  - Optional: VM OVA for highly regulated sites.

- Example Helm values (snippet):
  ```yaml
  global:
    imageRegistry: registry.redwood-inference.local
    tls:
      enabled: true
  controlPlane:
    replicas: 3
    resources:
      requests:
        cpu: "500m"
        memory: "1Gi"
  serving:
    gpuNodeCount: 4
    modelCache:
      path: /var/lib/redwood/models
      sizeGB: 2000
  ```

- Signing and verification:
  - All artifacts include a signed SBOM and sha256 manifest. For air-gapped installs supply the public key and verification script.

5) Day-2 operations: monitoring, backups, scaling:
- Observability:
  - Metrics: Prometheus metrics exported from model-serving (tokens/s, latency_p95, p99, gpu_utilization).
  - Traces: OTel-compatible tracing; sample rate configurable by env var.
  - Logs: structured JSON logs shipped to customer's ELK/CloudWatch.
  - Dashboards: pre-built Grafana dashboards for latency, token throughput, batch sizes, and per-model QPS.

- Backups & state management:
  - Recommended: nightly incremental backup of model artifact store metadata and weekly full snapshot.
  - Control plane state: export cluster configuration and agent registrations daily to secure S3/NFS.

- Autoscaling & capacity planning:
  - Horizontal scaling: add GPU nodes using cluster autoscaler with scale-out threshold at 70% GPU utilization for sustained 5m window.
  - Batching controls: configure max_batch_size and max_batch_latency via config map to tune cost vs latency.

6) Upgrade and rollback procedures (tested, repeatable):
- Goals: zero-downtime control-plane upgrade (canary first), safe model-serving rollout with automatic fallback.

Pre-upgrade checklist:
1. Take a full snapshot of config and control-plane state.
2. Ensure model artifact registry and keys are accessible.
3. Verify health of all nodes and confirm no active maintenance windows.
4. Notify stakeholders and schedule a 30-minute maintenance window if rollback may require intervention.

Canary upgrade (control plane):
1. Apply new Helm values with image tag (helm upgrade --install redwood-control ./chart -f values-canary.yaml).
2. Monitor control-plane logs and Prometheus metrics for 2x service interval (~10 minutes).
3. If errors > 0.5% or p99 latency increases by > 40% compared to baseline, abort and rollback to previous image (helm rollback).

Model-serving rollout (blue/green approach):
1. Create new node pool with upgraded runtime image.
2. Drain a small subset of old pool (10% of capacity) and move traffic to new pool via routing policy.
3. Run smoke tests against new nodes (inference samples, perf regressions, KV cache warmup).
4. If smoke tests fail, re-route traffic back and decommission new nodes; collect diagnostics and open an incident.

Rollback procedure (quick):
1. For control-plane regressions: helm rollback redwood-control --to-revision <prev>.
2. For serving regressions: update routing to previous node pool or scale previous image back up and drain new nodes.
3. Re-apply pre-upgrade snapshot if registry or state corruption is detected.

7) Runbook: common failure modes and mitigation (short):
- High p99 latency on inference:
  - Check GPU utilization and batch size; reduce max_batch_latency and/or increase node count.
  - Verify prefix cache hit rate (should be >80% for stable latency).
- Control-plane agent not registering:
  - Confirm control-plane endpoint reachable on port 8443 and TLS cert valid.
  - Check agent logs (/var/log/redwood/agent.log) for CA mismatch.
- Model pull failures in air-gapped sites:
  - Verify manifest signature and local OCI registry connectivity.
  - Re-run offline mirror tool and validate sha256 checks.

8) Safety & compliance guidance:
- Audit logging must be enabled for model deployments and configuration changes. Retain logs for a minimum of 90 days unless customer requires longer retention.
- For regulated customers, provide HSM integration plan and per-customer KMS keys. Record the key rotation policy and proof of rotation in the handover doc.

9) Handover & acceptance checklist (for go-live):
- Acceptance test suite results (functional and perf) uploaded to onboarding ticket.
- Security scans completed and passed (vuln scan of delivered images).
- 2 week support plan and runbook handed to customer's SRE with contacts.
- SLA & billing configuration confirmed.

10) Ownership, contacts and escalation:
- Owner: Private Deployments (eng-private-deployments)
- Primary support: Solutions Engineering (onboarding), Eng SRE (operational).
- Escalation path: on-call -> eng-sre -> platform -> eng-serving-runtime.

Appendices:
A. Ports & network table (summary):
- 8443 TCP: control-plane agent (TLS)
- 8000/8080 TCP: internal telemetry / metrics endpoints (cluster internal only)
- 2379 TCP: etcd (control-plane state) - restricted to control-plane subnets
- 443/80 TCP: optional registry/artifact proxy for air-gapped mirror

B. Example CLI commands:
- Helm install (cloud): helm upgrade --install redwood ./charts/redwood -f values.prod.yaml --namespace redwood
- Verify agent: kubectl -n redwood get pods -l app=redwood-agent
- Snapshot state: redwoodctl snapshot create --output s3://redwood-backups/customer-123/20261125

C. Troubleshooting artifacts to collect for support tickets:
- control-plane agent logs (last 2000 lines)
- serving node dmesg and nvidia-smi output
- prometheus query for last 15 minutes: rate(redwood_inference_tokens_total[15m])
- sha256 of model artifact and manifest file

If you are preparing a customer engagement, start with the Customer Requirements checklist above and run the pre-engagement network & security validation script (link in related artifacts). For questions or exceptions, contact eng-private-deployments@redwood-inference.internal.
